questions.text: Does its battery have one cell or more?

rules.ourWording: Flammable liquids can't go by international mail. That includes nail polish, hand sanitizer, and perfume or other liquids with alcohol.
The label says it is flammable. Flammable goods can't go by international mail.
Aerosols and other items under pressure can't go by international mail.
Alcoholic drinks can't be mailed.
Matches and lighters can't go by international mail.
E-cigarettes, vapes and e-liquids can't go by international mail.
Cigarettes and other tobacco can't go by international mail.
Cigars can go only to countries that accept them. Check that the country allows them.
Anything with mercury, such as an old thermometer or a CFL bulb, can't go by international mail.
Hemp and CBD products can't go by international mail.
Dry ice can't go by international mail.
Only very weak magnets can go by international mail. Check how strong this one is.
Most glues and many paints are flammable and can't go. Check the label for a flammable warning.
Lithium batteries must be inside the device they power. Spare batteries, batteries packed beside a device and power banks can't go.
Used devices with lithium batteries can't go by international mail. Only new or maker-refurbished ones can.
New devices are allowed in their original packaging. Pack this one back in its own box.
We can't see the battery rating through the box. Type the Wh from the box or the maker's page.
The battery numbers we read don't agree with each other. Check the label and type the numbers.
A lithium-ion cell above 20 Wh can't go by international mail.
A lithium-ion battery above 100 Wh can't go by international mail.
This has a lithium metal cell, such as a coin cell. We can't confirm how much lithium it holds, so check the maker's page.
A lithium metal cell with more than 1 g of lithium can't go by international mail.
A lithium metal battery with more than 2 g of lithium can't go by international mail.
Between 1 g and 2 g of lithium is allowed for a battery but not for a single cell. Say whether it has one cell or more.
Too many lithium batteries for one box. A box can hold 4 cells or 2 batteries, not both.
A box can hold 4 cells or 2 batteries, not both. This box may have both.
Don't put lithium battery marks or labels on the outside of the box.
No more than 2 boxes with lithium batteries can go to one address in one mailing.
We're not sure what this is. Fix the reading or type what it is.
Does the label list alcohol? Answer to finish this check.
Is it new? Answer to finish this check.
Where is the battery? Answer to finish this check.

CA.name: Canada

lines.ourWording: No alcoholic drinks, wine included.
No lighters with fuel in them. An empty new lighter is allowed.
Nothing that carries a flammable warning label.
No firearms.

noMatch.reason: Real firearms; toy and replica weapons are matched under CA-P-05.

lines.ourWording: No fake or inert munitions, or anything made to look like an explosive.
No vaping liquid with a high nicotine level.
No gold bullion, gold dust or raw precious metals.
No margarine or other butter substitutes.
No magazine issues whose ads mainly target Canada in the ways the listing describes.

noMatch.reason: Commercial magazine issues aimed at Canadian advertising; not a family gift.

lines.ourWording: That includes ads that say where in Canada to buy something.

noMatch.reason: Part of CA-P-09, which covers commercial magazine issues.

lines.ourWording: It also includes ads that give sale terms for Canada.

noMatch.reason: Part of CA-P-09, which covers commercial magazine issues.

lines.ourWording: No issue with a Canada-only ad that is missing from the home edition.

noMatch.reason: Commercial magazine issues with Canada-only ads; not a family gift.

lines.ourWording: No goods marked to look as if they were made in Canada or Britain when they were not.

noMatch.reason: A false made-in-Canada or made-in-Britain mark cannot be judged from a photo of a gift.

lines.ourWording: No metal trade tags.

noMatch.reason: Metal trade tags used by businesses; not a household gift.

lines.ourWording: No perishable biological material that can carry infection.

noMatch.reason: Infectious biological specimens such as lab samples; never a household gift.

lines.ourWording: No other perishable biological material.

noMatch.reason: Other perishable biological specimens such as lab samples; never a household gift.

lines.ourWording: No feathers or skins of wild birds.

noMatch.reason: Wild bird feathers and skins; down in clothing comes from farmed birds and is not matched.

lines.ourWording: No prison-made goods for sale.

noMatch.reason: Goods made in prisons for sale; not a family gift.

lines.ourWording: No radioactive material.

noMatch.reason: Radioactive material; USPS already bars it from international mail.

lines.ourWording: No reprints of works under Canadian copyright.

noMatch.reason: Whether a book is an unlicensed reprint cannot be judged from a photo.

lines.ourWording: No copies of Canadian stamps, except black and white prints that are crossed out.

noMatch.reason: Whether a stamp image is a banned reproduction cannot be judged from a photo.

lines.ourWording: No smoke-making devices for cars or boats.

noMatch.reason: Smoke-making devices for cars and boats; not a household gift.

lines.ourWording: No used beehives or bee supplies.

noMatch.reason: Used beehives and bee supplies; not a household gift.

lines.ourWording: Valuables such as jewelry, gems, cash or gold can go only in an insured parcel.
Medicines must meet Canadian law.
Hatching eggs need new packing and a vet certificate.

noMatch.reason: Eggs for hatching; never a household gift.

lines.ourWording: Meat products need a US export certificate and Canadian labels.
Samples under 10 kg are an exception.

noMatch.reason: An exception to the meat rule CA-R-04, for trade samples.

lines.ourWording: So is meat sent to a government office.

noMatch.reason: An exception to the meat rule CA-R-04, for government offices.

lines.ourWording: So is meat the importer carries in for their own use.

noMatch.reason: An exception to the meat rule CA-R-04, for a person carrying meat in.

lines.ourWording: Some pet foods with raw ingredients need an import permit and a health certificate.
Animal vaccines and serums need a permit from Canada.

noMatch.reason: Animal vaccines and serums; not a household gift.

lines.ourWording: Gifts by mail worth under 60 Canadian dollars come in free of duty and tax.

noMatch.reason: A duty and tax note; shown to the sender as a customs note.

lines.ourWording: Canada turns away items without a full sender and recipient address in Latin letters and Arabic numerals.

noMatch.reason: An address rule; shown to the sender as a customs note.

lines.ourWording: The address must include the province.

noMatch.reason: An address rule; shown to the sender as a customs note.

customsNotes: Put a card or note in the box saying it is a gift.
Gifts worth under 60 Canadian dollars come in free of duty and tax.
Write the full sender and recipient addresses, including the province.

PH.name: Philippines

lines.ourWording: No liquids, nothing that turns runny easily, and nothing made of glass or as fragile as glass.
No coins, cash, bearer securities, traveler's checks, precious metals, gems or other valuables.
No guns or other weapons, their parts, ammunition, or copies of weapons.
No gambling devices.

noMatch.reason: Gambling devices such as slot machines; not something this app reads in a gift box.

lines.ourWording: No lottery tickets or lottery advertising.

noMatch.reason: Lottery tickets and lottery advertising; not a gift category this app reads.

lines.ourWording: No narcotics or similar drugs.

noMatch.reason: Controlled narcotics; ordinary medicines are tagged and checked by other rules.

lines.ourWording: No perishable biological material that can carry infection.

noMatch.reason: Infectious biological specimens such as lab samples; never a household gift.

lines.ourWording: No other perishable biological material.

noMatch.reason: Other perishable biological specimens such as lab samples; never a household gift.

lines.ourWording: No radioactive material.

noMatch.reason: Radioactive material; USPS already bars it from international mail.

lines.ourWording: Coffee is allowed for personal use only, up to 2 kg of beans or ground coffee.
Plants and similar items need import clearance and plant health certificates.
An invoice with a duty value of 3,000 pesos or more may need the Philippine Consulate's stamp, for a $30 fee.

noMatch.reason: An invoice and duty note; shown to the sender as a customs note.

customsNotes: If the box is worth 3,000 pesos or more in duty value, the invoice may need the Philippine Consulate's stamp and a $30 fee.
